headings.title: Establishment of Department of Mental Health
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Department of Mental Health headed by a commission appointing a director with senate confirmation and merit system staffing.

headings.title: State Mental Health Commission composition and terms
headings.reviewNote: Establishes seven-member commission, staggered four-year terms, and required expertise in mental illness, developmental disabilities, business, and substance abuse.

headings.title: Transfer of powers from welfare department
headings.reviewNote: Transfers division of mental health powers, duties, and statutory functions by type I transfer from the department of public health and welfare and abolishes the prior division (source footnote notes repealed sections 191.120, 191.125, 191.130, 191.140, and 191.200).

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri Institute of Mental Health
headings.reviewNote: Renames Missouri Institute of Psychiatry, defines research and training missions with University curators, and separates budget submissions.

headings.title: Establishment of division of developmental disabilities
headings.reviewNote: Creates division of developmental disabilities, directs appointment of division director, and transfers state habilitation and regional centers.

headings.title: Transfer of advisory council on mental retardation
headings.reviewNote: Transfers advisory council on mental retardation and community health centers to the division of developmental disabilities by type I transfer.

headings.title: Transfer of advisory council on developmental disabilities
headings.reviewNote: Transfers executive order advisory council and federal developmental disabilities responsibilities to the division by type I transfer.

headings.title: Transfer of advisory council on alcoholism
headings.reviewNote: Transfers advisory council on alcoholism and drug abuse to the department by type II transfer with member appointment by director.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Department of Mental Health, Mental Health Commission, division transfers, Missouri Institute of Mental Health, and advisory councils.

headings.title: Commission composition and term lengths
headings.reviewNote: Specifies seven members appointed by the governor with senate consent for four-year terms and continuation until successor qualification.

headings.title: Professional qualifications and consumer representation
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission composition including medical specialists, disability clinicians, consumers, families, business experts, and substance abuse specialists.

headings.title: Filling of commission vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Directs gubernatorial appointments with senate consent for unexpired terms and temporary recess appointments until the next legislative session.

headings.title: Election of officers and meeting frequency
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission election of chairman and secretary, monthly regular meetings, and special meetings on call of the chairman.

headings.title: Per diem compensation and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides one hundred dollars per diem compensation plus actual necessary expense reimbursement for commissioners transacting official business.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs State Mental Health Commission membership qualifications, term lengths, vacancies, officers, meetings, and per diem compensation.

headings.title: Appointment and tenure of department director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state mental health commission to appoint the department director with senate advice and consent to serve at the commission's pleasure.

headings.title: Advisory duties regarding professional standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to advise the director on treatment facilities, staff recruitment, training, medical records, and service accessibility.

headings.title: Advisory role in mental health research
headings.reviewNote: Tasks the commission with advising the director on initiating, approving, and guiding research projects and allocating research funds.

headings.title: Assistance with plans and program reviews
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to assist the director in maintaining and reviewing plans, rules, programs, and facilities operated or licensed by the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines State Mental Health Commission duties regarding director appointment, professional standards advice, research funding, and program review.

headings.title: Statutory purposes and goals of department
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to reduce disorder incidence through prevention, provide habilitation in the least restrictive environment, and improve public understanding.

headings.title: Administrative orders and operating procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to make necessary orders, policies, and procedures for the government, administration, discipline, and management of its facilities, programs, and operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Sets department goals for prevention, least restrictive habilitation, public understanding, and internal administration orders.

headings.title: Director salary limits and outside income ban
headings.reviewNote: Provides that commission sets director salary within appropriations and prohibits outside consulting income except professional publications.

headings.title: Official oath of department director
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to take a constitutional oath of office before assuming official administrative duties.

headings.title: Director as chief executive officer
headings.reviewNote: Designates the director as chief executive officer exercising all administrative powers and duties conferred by law.

headings.title: Gubernatorial requests for internal reorganization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to request the governor to reorganize internal departmental organization pursuant to state executive reorganization statutes.

headings.title: Investigative hearings and witness subpoena authority
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the director to conduct inquiries, hold administrative hearings, subpoena witnesses and records, administer oaths, and compensate witnesses.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes powers, salary limitations, official oath, executive authority, reorganization requests, and subpoena powers of the department director.

headings.title: Appointment of facility chief administrative officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires division directors, with department director approval, to appoint chief administrative officers for division facilities in accordance with chapter 36.

headings.title: Appointment of medical chiefs of staff
headings.reviewNote: Requires major department facilities to have licensed physician chiefs of staff responsible for developing and monitoring medical treatment.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides for merit appointment of facility chief administrative officers and appointment of licensed medical chiefs of staff.

headings.title: Facility management by chief administrative officer
headings.reviewNote: Vests charge, control, and management of department facilities in chief administrative officers subject to departmental directives.

headings.title: Record keeping and reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires chief administrative officers to maintain records and prepare necessary reports as directed by the department and division.

headings.title: Merit appointing authority of facility officers
headings.reviewNote: Empowers chief administrative officers to exercise chapter 36 appointing authority subject to departmental supervision.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines management powers, record keeping, and merit appointing authority of facility chief administrative officers.

headings.title: Rulemaking for funding, licensing, and abuse
headings.reviewNote: Directs promulgation of rules for fees, funding, facility licensing, and abuse investigations under administrative procedure statutes.

headings.title: Internal operating regulations exempt from publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to adopt internal management operating regulations exempt from Missouri Register and CSR publication but available for public inspection at department facilities.

headings.title: Facility internal management policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires each facility, under department and division supervision, to adopt internal management and client procedure policies exempt from chapter 536 publication but available on site for public inspection.

headings.title: Compatibility of rules with facility mission
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules, operating regulations, and facility policies to remain compatible with facility mission, size, and population served.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs department rulemaking for licensing and abuse reporting, internal operating regulations, facility policies, and compatibility standards.

headings.title: Establishment of Mental Health Earnings Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the nonreverting Mental Health Earnings Fund in the state treasury and credits investment interest to the fund.

headings.title: Deposit and dedication of SATOP fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires deposit of substance abuse traffic offender fees solely for rehabilitation services for individuals unable to pay.

headings.title: Deposit of managed care agreement revenues
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes separate accounting and expenditure of managed care revenues for agreement services subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Revenues from counselor certification oversight
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deposit and separate accounting of revenues from agreements with counselor certification boards for credentialing oversight.

headings.title: Deposit of Mental Health First Aid proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes deposit of proceeds from sales and services to fund Mental Health First Aid USA activities upon appropriation approval.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for earnings fund administration
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules and regulations to implement and administer earnings fund provisions under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Mental Health Earnings Fund in the state treasury, regulates SATOP fees, managed care deposits, and counselor certification funds.

headings.title: Community participation and public education programs
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to encourage community participation and develop public information programs regarding mental health and disabilities.

headings.title: Interagency and foundation educational contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes direct contracts with government entities and the Missouri Mental Health Foundation for public education exempt from chapter 34.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs community participation programs, public education on mental disabilities, and direct contracts with public agencies and foundations.

headings.title: Workers' compensation coverage for department personnel
headings.reviewNote: Extends chapter 287 coverage to employees, students, and volunteer workers under state self-insurance defended by the attorney general.

headings.title: Administrative authority of department director
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department director to perform necessary administrative duties to carry out workers' compensation protections.

headings.title: Limitation on state tort liability
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that extending workers' compensation protections shall not be construed as creating state tort liability.

entries.reviewSummary: Extends workers' compensation coverage to department employees and volunteer workers under state self-insurance, limiting tort liability.

headings.title: Annual written report to governor and legislature
headings.reviewNote: Mandates an annual written departmental report to the governor and general assembly within ninety days of fiscal year end.

headings.title: Cost effectiveness and financial accounting contents
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports to detail cost-benefit effectiveness, program accomplishments, financial receipts, and expenditures for each division.

headings.title: Biennial facility standards compliance report
headings.reviewNote: Requires even-numbered year reporting on facility standards compliance, citing deficiencies and corrective actions needed.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires an annual written report to the governor and general assembly and biennial reporting on facility standards compliance.

headings.title: Receipt and administration of federal grants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department upon gubernatorial designation to receive, administer, and disburse federal grants under program conditions.

headings.title: Director approval of federal assistance applications
headings.reviewNote: Requires director approval of federal aid applications following consultations with division directors and state advisory councils.

headings.title: Federal reporting and minimum operating standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires compliance reports and establishment of minimum operating standards for facilities and programs receiving grant funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes receipt and administration of federal grants, director approval of applications, and establishment of facility standards.

headings.title: Comprehensive System Management Team and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department and children's services commission partners to develop a unified children's mental health system, establish the ten-member-category Comprehensive System Management Team and stakeholder advisory committee, and promulgate implementation rules.

headings.title: State comprehensive children's mental health plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires developing and submitting a ten-element state comprehensive children's mental health service system plan by December 2004, followed by annual progress reports.

headings.title: Collaboration on uniform intake and service language
headings.reviewNote: Directs the comprehensive system management team to collaborate to develop uniform language for use in intake and throughout service provision.

headings.title: Core service system design principles
headings.reviewNote: Specifies system principles including child-centered care, least restrictive community settings, evidence-based practices, and early intervention.

headings.title: Legislative evaluation of child mental health
headings.reviewNote: Requires the children's services commission to submit periodic evaluations of child mental health services to the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates an interagency comprehensive child mental health plan, management team collaboration, system principles, and legislative evaluation.

headings.title: Establishment of Office of Comprehensive Child Mental Health
headings.reviewNote: Creates the office to oversee implementation of the child mental health plan, provide technical assistance, and coordinate policy.

headings.title: Department representation on system management team
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating state departments to designate staff representatives to serve on the state comprehensive system management team.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Office of Comprehensive Child Mental Health, defining oversight duties, clinical consultation, and management team leadership.

headings.title: Establishment and multidisciplinary membership of council
headings.reviewNote: Creates the advisory council within the department comprising up to ten multidisciplinary specialists, with director serving ex officio.

headings.title: Member appointments, expenses, and advisory responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Provides three-year terms, expense reimbursement, and duties to share clinical trends, liaison with disciplines, and identify funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Comprehensive Child Mental Health Clinical Advisory Council, defining multidisciplinary membership, terms, and advisory duties.

headings.title: Guidelines for assessing medical causes of behavior
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop screening guidelines addressing physical and mental health interactions causing behavioral changes.

headings.title: Limitation to state-owned and operated facilities
headings.reviewNote: Restricts applicability of physical-mental assessment guidelines to state-owned or operated facilities, exempting licensed hospitals.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to administer assessment guidelines subject to chapter 536 statutory nonseverability provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires guidelines for screening physical and medical causes of behavioral changes in state-operated mental health facilities, with rules.

headings.title: Statutory civil rights of facility residents
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees rights to wear personal clothing, keep money, send mail, receive visitors, use telephones, and access medical records.

headings.title: Documentation of rights limitations in clinical record
headings.reviewNote: Requires clinical record documentation of any therapeutic limitations placed on patient personal rights and the reasons therefor.

headings.title: Absolute right to private professional visits
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees each patient an absolute right to private visits at reasonable times with legal counsel, physicians, or clergy.

headings.title: Unrestricted sealed mail communication rights
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees patient rights to communicate by sealed mail with the department, legal counsel, and the court of jurisdiction.

headings.title: Rights restrictions for committed criminal defendants
headings.reviewNote: Restricts personal property, mail, and telephone rights for criminal commitments and sexually violent predators absent safety clearance.

entries.reviewSummary: Enumerates statutory civil rights for mental health facility residents, clinical limitation documentation, and attorney communication rights.

headings.title: Fundamental patient rights and treatment protections
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees fifteen unconditional patient rights including humane care, safe housing, least restrictive environment, research and surgical consent, diet, and freedom from abuse (source footnote notes 'season' appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Right to impartial administrative grievance review
headings.reviewNote: Provides patients with rights to impartial administrative reviews, grievance hearings before neutral decision makers, and written findings.

headings.title: Timely completion of administrative grievance review
headings.reviewNote: Requires that the impartial administrative review process be completed in a timely manner following receipt of grievance reports.

headings.title: Exemption for patient abuse and neglect investigations
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the administrative grievance review process does not apply to abuse and neglect investigations under section 630.167.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes fundamental patient rights, least restrictive treatment, nourishment standards, and impartial administrative grievance reviews.

headings.title: Interagency project on unjustified foster hospitalization
headings.reviewNote: Directs mental health and social services to assess medically unjustified hospitalizations of foster children and recommend solutions.

headings.title: Stakeholder data collection and consultation
headings.reviewNote: Requires departments to solicit data from foster youth, clients, hospital discharge planners, insurers, facilities, and courts.

headings.title: Interim and final legislative reporting deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Requires submission of interim reports in 2023 and 2024 and a final report to the general assembly by December 1, 2024.

headings.title: Statutory expiration date of hospitalization project
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the collaborative foster hospitalization study project provisions shall expire on January 1, 2025.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs a collaborative interagency project on unjustified hospitalizations of foster children and mental health clients, sunsetting in 2025.

headings.title: Written rights and service information upon admission
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to provide admitting patients lay-language written information detailing services, costs, discharge procedures, rights, and grievances.

headings.title: Oral explanation of admission information
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility personnel to explain admission information orally if the patient cannot read with full understanding.

headings.title: Prominent posting of patient rights
headings.reviewNote: Mandates prominent posting of patient and residential rights lists in residential and activity areas of facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires written patient rights and release information upon admission, oral explanations, and prominent posting of rights.

headings.title: Initial guardian notification of offender placement risks
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules for initial notification informing guardians of the potential placement of registered sex offenders or incompetent offenders in facilities.

headings.title: Risk assessment and safety mitigation protocols
headings.reviewNote: Requires safety planning, risk mitigation services, and consultation mechanisms for parents or guardians concerning offender placements.

headings.title: Notification of registered sex offender co-residence
headings.reviewNote: Directs rules requiring specific notification to guardians prior to or upon co-residence of registered sex offenders in facilities.

headings.title: Consent protocols for disclosing incompetent offender status
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules and protocols to seek consent from parents, guardians, or self-guardian consumers under subsection 1(2) to disclose their name and criminal charges to other facility parents, guardians, or consumers, without refusal preventing placement.

headings.title: Chapter 536 compliance for promulgated rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that any rule or portion of a rule created under this section becomes effective only if it complies with chapter 536 and, if applicable, section 536.028.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs rules and protocols for guardian notification of registered sex offender and incompetent offender placements, risk mitigation, disclosure consent, and chapter 536 compliance.

headings.title: Right to refuse electroconvulsive therapy
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees voluntary and involuntary mental health patients the absolute right to refuse electroconvulsive therapy.

headings.title: Informed consent for voluntary electroconvulsive therapy
headings.reviewNote: Requires detailed oral and written disclosure of risks and documented informed consent before voluntary electroconvulsive therapy is administered.

headings.title: Court order requirements for involuntary therapy
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes involuntary electroconvulsive therapy only pursuant to court order following a full evidentiary hearing with legal representation.

headings.title: Court orders for minor and incompetent patients
headings.reviewNote: Requires parents of minors and guardians of incompetent patients to obtain court orders authorizing electroconvulsive therapy.

headings.title: Prohibition on electroconvulsive therapy for intellectual disability
headings.reviewNote: Explicitly prohibits electroconvulsive therapy for individuals diagnosed solely as intellectually disabled.

headings.title: State payment of attorney's fees for indigent respondents
headings.reviewNote: Requires the judge to allow a reasonable attorney's fee paid as costs by the state when an indigent respondent cannot pay, excluding salaried employees of public or publicly funded agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates right to refuse electroconvulsive therapy, informed consent, court order requirements, intellectual disability bar, and attorney fees.

headings.title: Prohibition on involuntary psychosurgery and consent requirements
headings.reviewNote: Bans involuntary psychosurgery on any patient and mandates full risk disclosure and written consent for competent patients.

headings.title: Absolute prohibition in department facilities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits psychosurgery from being performed by the department in any facility operated by the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits involuntary psychosurgery, requires written informed consent, and bans psychosurgery in all department facilities.

headings.title: Confidentiality of mental health records and files
headings.reviewNote: Classifies all patient information, records, and communications as confidential and exempt from open public records disclosure.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure to patients, guardians, and counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to disclose records including medications and dosages upon request to patients, guardians, attorneys, or parents of minors.

headings.title: Permissive disclosure of records and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes record disclosures pursuant to patient authorization, treatment coordination, insurance reimbursement, research protocols, or court orders.

headings.title: Documentation of record disclosures in clinical files
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to document the date, nature, purpose, and recipient of any disclosed confidential patient records.

headings.title: Confidentiality of civil commitment court records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies chapter 632 court records as confidential and limits access to the patient, counsel, guardian or parent, petitioner and counsel, highway patrol for NICS reporting, community mental health liaisons, or by court order for good cause.

headings.title: Preservation of judicial and administrative discovery rights
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that statutory mental health confidentiality does not limit judicial or administrative discovery rights under law.

headings.title: Restrictions on disclosing fact of admission
headings.reviewNote: Restricts disclosure of the fact of voluntary or involuntary admission to authorized representatives or permitted statutory disclosures.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes confidentiality of mental health records, mandatory disclosures to clients and attorneys, permissive disclosures, and court records.

headings.title: Release of general health information to relatives
headings.reviewNote: Permits releasing to next of kin, attorney, guardian, or conservator that a person is a patient, resident, or client or is seriously physically ill, and requires notifying them or cost-responsible persons of a voluntary patient's admittance.

headings.title: Mandatory notification of patient death and cause
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to notify next of kin, guardians, or conservators immediately upon the death of a patient and state the cause.

headings.title: Priority order of next of kin notification
headings.reviewNote: Establishes next-of-kin notification order unless otherwise indicated: spouse, parents, children, brothers and sisters, and other relatives by degree of relation.

headings.title: Patient designation of additional emergency contacts
headings.reviewNote: Allows patients or residents to designate additional persons to be notified in the event of death, serious injury, or incapacity.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes release of condition updates to next of kin, death notifications, priority order of relatives, and patient designated contacts.

headings.title: Notification of unauthorized disappearance from facility
headings.reviewNote: Permits disclosing notice of unauthorized disappearance or unknown whereabouts with relevant information to relatives, law enforcement, and other designated persons when necessary for protection.

headings.title: Notification procedures for criminal commitment disappearances
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate notice of disappearance of a chapter 552 committed person to prosecutors and sheriffs of the detention and trial counties, known surviving chapter 595 victims, and other necessary agencies or persons.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs notification to law enforcement, guardians, and next of kin upon unauthorized patient disappearance, and special notices for criminal commitments.

headings.title: Definition of patient abuse and neglect offenses
headings.reviewNote: Defines patient, resident, or client abuse or neglect as knowingly beating or injuring, brutal or inhuman mistreatment, excessive force, or failing to provide reasonable and necessary services presenting imminent danger or substantial probability of death or serious physical harm.

headings.title: Misdemeanor and felony penalties for abuse
headings.reviewNote: Classifies patient, resident, or client abuse or neglect as a class A misdemeanor, or a class E felony when committed under subdivision (2) or (4) of subsection 1.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines offenses of patient abuse and neglect in mental health facilities, establishing misdemeanor penalties and felony classifications.

headings.title: Prohibition on furnishing unfit food to patients
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to knowingly deliver diseased meat, putrid food, or unwholesome provisions to mental health facilities or patients.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for furnishing unfit food
headings.reviewNote: Classifies the offense of furnishing unfit food to mental health patients, residents, or clients as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Criminalizes furnishing diseased or unwholesome food to mental health facility patients and classifies offenses as misdemeanors.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of vulnerable person abuse
headings.reviewNote: Requires designated healthcare professionals, facility personnel, law enforcement, and caregivers to report suspected abuse or neglect of vulnerable persons.

headings.title: Sanctions for facility prevention of abuse reporting
headings.reviewNote: Subjects facilities discouraging or preventing abuse reporting to license revocation and civil fines up to five thousand dollars per violation.

headings.title: Exemption for religious beliefs and spiritual prayer
headings.reviewNote: Provides that reliance on spiritual healing through prayer does not solely constitute abuse or neglect of a vulnerable person.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates abuse reporting for vulnerable persons, bans facility interference under civil fines, and provides spiritual treatment exemptions.

headings.title: Reporting abuse or neglect of vulnerable persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons suspecting abuse or neglect of vulnerable persons to report to the department and forwards interagency reports.

headings.title: Required oral and written report contents
headings.reviewNote: Specifies report contents including vulnerable person identifying information, caregiver details, condition of the person, and relevant facts.

headings.title: Primary department responsibility for investigations
headings.reviewNote: Vests primary responsibility in the department for investigating reported incidents of abuse and neglect of vulnerable persons.

headings.title: Referral of non-vulnerable person reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs referral of reports concerning individuals who are not vulnerable persons to appropriate state or local authorities.

headings.title: Collaborative statewide toll-free hotline
headings.reviewNote: Requires interagency collaboration with health and social services to maintain a centralized statewide toll-free reporting hotline.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs reporting of vulnerable person abuse, report contents, department investigation primacy, non-vulnerable referrals, and toll-free hotline.

headings.title: Mandatory abuse reporting by healthcare personnel
headings.reviewNote: Requires designated healthcare professionals, facility personnel, direct-care workers, and social workers to immediately report suspected patient abuse.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for failure to report abuse
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing failure to report suspected abuse or neglect as a class A misdemeanor punishable by fine up to one thousand dollars.

headings.title: Felony penalty for subsequent failure to report
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a subsequent conviction for failing to make a required report after a prior conviction or guilty plea as a class E felony with a fine up to five thousand dollars payable to the state school moneys fund.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for knowingly filing false report
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowingly filing a false report of vulnerable person abuse or neglect as a class A misdemeanor with a fine up to one thousand dollars payable to the state school moneys fund.

headings.title: Felony penalty for subsequent false abuse report
headings.reviewNote: Classifies a subsequent conviction for making a false report after a prior conviction or guilty plea as a class E felony with a fine up to five thousand dollars payable to the state school moneys fund.

headings.title: Court determination of prior false-reporting convictions
headings.reviewNote: Requires evidence of prior false-reporting convictions to be heard and determined by the court out of the hearing of the jury before submission of the case.

headings.title: License loss and fines for discouraging reporting
headings.reviewNote: Subjects facilities, day programs, or specialized services preventing or discouraging abuse or neglect reporting to loss of license under sections 630.705 to 630.760 and civil fines up to five thousand dollars per attempt.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates suspected abuse and neglect reporting, establishes misdemeanor and repeat-offender felony penalties for failure to report and false reports, and penalizes facilities that discourage reporting.

headings.title: Initiation of patient abuse investigations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department or health department to initiate prompt on-site investigations upon receiving reports of patient abuse or neglect.

headings.title: Director referral and ex parte temporary removal orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires investigators to refer reports of possible abuse or neglect to the department director and authorizes circuit court petitions (mandatory for the attorney general upon department request) for ex parte temporary care and protection orders up to thirty days.

headings.title: Confidentiality and restricted disclosure of reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies abuse reports and investigations as confidential nonpublic records, specifying authorized disclosure to law enforcement and victims.

headings.title: Civil immunity for reporting and testifying
headings.reviewNote: Shields persons making abuse reports or testifying in administrative or judicial proceedings from civil liability absent bad faith.

headings.title: Notice to reporter and guardian in neglect cases
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice to the reporter within five working days of receipt and initiation, and requires notifying the guardian in neglect investigations of the investigation and results within five working days of completion.

headings.title: Independent reviews of investigated patient deaths
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department of mental health to obtain two independent reviews of all patient, resident, or client deaths that it investigates.

headings.title: Prohibition on facility retaliation against victims
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits facility administrators from evicting, harassing, or retaliating against patients, residents, or employees making reports or cooperating.

headings.title: Circuit court appeals for discharged merit employees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes section 36.030(1)(2) employees discharged for substantiated abuse or neglect, after exhausting chapter 36 remedies, to appeal to circuit court within ninety days, or up to twenty-four months upon a three-part showing.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates abuse investigations, reports, confidentiality, civil immunity, notice to reporters, independent death reviews, and employee protections.

headings.title: Disqualification from employment in facilities
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies persons listed on the department disqualification registry or other state employee registries from employment in facilities.

headings.title: Disqualifying criminal felony and person offenses
headings.reviewNote: Lists disqualifying felony convictions including drug offenses, crimes against persons, sex offenses, sexual assault, and robbery.

headings.title: Disqualification following suspended imposition of sentence
headings.reviewNote: Applies employment disqualification to individuals receiving suspended impositions or executions of sentence for disqualifying crimes.

headings.title: Director exception waivers for disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes disqualified individuals to apply to the director for an exception waiver upon demonstrating good cause and rehabilitation.

headings.title: Applicant criminal disclosures and consent forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants for facility positions to sign consent forms disclosing criminal histories and authorizes registry background checks.

headings.title: Reciprocity for health department waivers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that individuals holding valid good cause waivers from health and senior services do not require additional mental health waivers.

headings.title: Post-hire criminal and registry check requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires covered facilities and programs, within two working days after hiring a person for client-contact work, to request a section 43.540 criminal check and inquire on the DHSS/DSS employee disqualification list and DMH disqualification registry.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for false disclosure and hiring
headings.reviewNote: Classifies applicant failure to disclose criminal records or provider knowing employment of disqualified individuals as class A misdemeanors.

headings.title: Employer immunity for declining or discharging disqualified staff
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from suit to covered facilities and programs that decline to employ or discharge a person disqualified under subsection 1 or 2.

headings.title: Unemployment charge exemption for required discharge
headings.reviewNote: Exempts employers required to discharge an employee placed on the DMH disqualification registry after hire from section 288.100 unemployment insurance benefit charges for prior wages.

headings.title: Maintenance of employee disqualification registry
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to maintain a centralized registry of individuals disqualified from employment due to substantiated abuse.

headings.title: Notice and administrative appeal of registry listing
headings.reviewNote: Allows notified persons to appeal registry placement under department rules and bars the hearing tribunal from modifying listing duration if it upholds all substantiations, while permitting modification if part is overturned.

headings.title: Determination of registry listing duration
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to determine the duration of listing on the registry based on abuse severity and previous history.

headings.title: Interagency and federal registry data sharing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to share disqualification registry records with other state, federal, and licensed provider agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes employment disqualification registry, criminal bars, exception waivers, pre-employment screening, penalties, and appeals.

headings.title: Prohibition on restraints and emergency exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits physical restraint, chemical restraint, isolation, or seclusion except in emergency circumstances to protect the patient or others.

headings.title: Clinical documentation of restraint or seclusion
headings.reviewNote: Requires detailed clinical record documentation of the medical justification and duration of any restraint, isolation, or seclusion.

headings.title: Immediate cessation of emergency restraints
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that restraint or seclusion is not standard treatment and must cease immediately when the causing emergency terminates.

headings.title: Exemption for security transport escort devices
headings.reviewNote: Exempts physical escort devices used to maintain safety and prevent escape during transit from restraint restrictions.

headings.title: Extraordinary safety measures during emergencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary extraordinary security measures during natural disasters or facility emergencies to protect patient and public safety.

headings.title: Physician review of collaborative practice restraint orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires in-person review by the attending licensed physician within twenty-four hours or the next regular working day, documented in the clinical record, for restraint orders issued by an APRN, PA, or assistant physician.

headings.title: Restraint and seclusion limits in developmental programs
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits restraint or seclusion in division of developmental disabilities habilitation centers or community programs unless part of a division-approved emergency intervention system identified in the individual support plan, and requires direct-care staff training.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits physical or chemical restraints and seclusion except in emergencies, regulates medical orders, and bans seclusion in habilitation centers.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of review committee
headings.reviewNote: Creates a ten-member Professional Review Committee appointed by the director to review and recommend research proposals in facilities.

headings.title: Per diem compensation and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides one hundred dollars per day compensation plus actual necessary expense reimbursement for committee members performing official duties.

headings.title: Annual officer elections and meeting quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual election of a chairman, meetings on call of the director, and establishes a quorum of at least five members.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Professional Review Committee to evaluate biomedical and pharmacological research proposals, set compensation, and govern meetings.

headings.title: Submission of research proposals to committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires researchers seeking to conduct biomedical or pharmacological studies in department facilities to submit proposals to the committee.

headings.title: Monitoring and suspension of research projects
headings.reviewNote: Directs ongoing monitoring of research projects and authorizes project suspension if risk of harm increases or protocols are breached.

headings.title: Evaluation criteria for biomedical research proposals
headings.reviewNote: Establishes proposal review criteria including medical necessity, sound research design, safety protections, and clinical ethics.

headings.title: Consultation with outside scientific experts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the committee to retain independent outside experts to review specialized research proposals and recommend disposition.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes submission procedures, progress reviews, scientific criteria, and expert consultations for biomedical and pharmacological research.

headings.title: Establishment of facility research review committees
headings.reviewNote: Creates a five-member Research Review Committee at each facility proposing to conduct biomedical or pharmacological research.

headings.title: Staggered terms for research committee members
headings.reviewNote: Provides four-year member terms with initial terms staggered to ensure continuity of committee oversight.

headings.title: Reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation but receive reimbursement for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Annual chairman election and meeting quorum
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual chairman election, meetings on call of the facility head or chairman, and a three-member quorum (source footnote notes 'are' does not appear in original rolls).

entries.reviewSummary: Creates facility Research Review Committees, establishing five-member compositions, four-year terms, expenses, and meeting procedures.

headings.title: Competency determinations for research participants
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility committees to determine that persons selected to participate in biomedical research are competent to give consent.

headings.title: Mandatory criteria for valid informed consent
headings.reviewNote: Requires committees to assure that informed consent reflects capacity to understand risks, benefits, and procedures, sufficient information, and free volition without coercive influence.

headings.title: Right to refuse or withdraw from research
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees that participants may refuse to participate or withdraw from research projects at any time without penalty.

headings.title: Compensation of participants in research projects
headings.reviewNote: Requires research subjects to be compensated for their time to the same extent as non-patient participants in similar research.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates participant competency determinations, informed consent standards, voluntary withdrawal rights, and participant research compensation.

headings.title: Definitions for essential caregiver provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, essential caregiver, and facility for section 630.202.

headings.title: Designation of essential caregiver during emergency
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities during a chapter 44 disease state of emergency to allow residents, clients, guardians, or authorized representatives to designate an essential caregiver as part of the care team for in-person contact.

headings.title: Written notice of essential caregiver program
headings.reviewNote: Requires facilities to inform residents, clients, guardians, or legal representatives in writing of the essential caregiver program and designation process.

headings.title: Minimum requirements for caregiver visitation policies
headings.reviewNote: Requires designation of two caregivers, at least four hours daily in-person contact, safety protocols, and weekly limitation reviews.

headings.title: Facility suspension requests and state legal defense
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary seven-day visitation suspensions for serious health risks and directs attorney general to defend state visitation rights.

headings.title: Voluntary nature of caregiver services
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that essential caregivers are not required to provide necessary care and facilities shall not mandate caregiver services.

headings.title: Exemption for unrelated therapeutic treatment restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Exempts residents whose individual therapeutic plans require restricted visitation for reasons unrelated to declared emergencies.

headings.title: Civil liability immunity for participating facilities
headings.reviewNote: Shields facilities, employees, and contractors from civil liability for specified disease exposure or essential caregiver acts or omissions, excluding recklessness or willful misconduct.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines essential caregiver terms, guarantees in-person caregiver access during chapter 44 disease emergencies, sets visitation standards and suspension limits, and grants facility civil immunity.

headings.title: Joint and several liability and subrogation rights
headings.reviewNote: Establishes joint and several liability for service fees, exempts parents of adult residents, and subrogates the department to damage awards.

headings.title: Exemption for special education and residential costs
headings.reviewNote: Exempts parents of Missouri minors from costs of special education, related services, and nonmedical room and board under IEP placements.

headings.title: Definition of special education and services
headings.reviewNote: Defines special education and related services by reference to federal education statutes and implementing regulations.

headings.title: Prohibition on service denial for inability to pay
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits denying department facility services to Missouri domiciled residents due to an inability to pay fees.

headings.title: Preservation of third party and insurer liability
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that fee liability provisions do not relieve health insurers or other third parties from valid payment obligations.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes joint and several liability for facility fees, subrogation rights, minor education expense exemptions, and third party liability.

headings.title: Determination of maximum service charges
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to determine maximum service charges based on per capita costs and promulgate rules establishing a standard means test.

headings.title: Means test application, retroactivity, and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual and permits discretionary application of the standard means test, allows retroactive charge adjustments for noncooperation or retroactive benefits, makes the director's decision final, and provides chapter 536 circuit court appeals.

headings.title: Non-domiciliary payment limits and transient exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits department payment for non-Missouri domiciliaries without full reimbursement, permits up to thirty days for transients pending verification or emergencies, and directs domiciliary-determination rules.

headings.title: Discharge for nonpayment stayed pending appeal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes chapter 31 discharge of a patient, resident, or client when responsible parties fail to pay support installments, stayed until final disposition of any subsection 2 appeal.

headings.title: Waiver of means test for children and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Permits waiving the standard means test for a child needing mental health services to avoid inappropriate children's division custody transfers, requires parent notice, and directs chapter 536 nonseverability rulemaking (after August 28, 2004).

entries.reviewSummary: Governs maximum facility service charges, standard means test application and appeals, non-domiciliary payment limits, chapter 31 discharge for nonpayment, and child means-test waivers.

headings.title: Probate court estate notice and means test
headings.reviewNote: Requires probate divisions with knowledge of a patient's, resident's, or client's estate to notify the director of the estate, attorney, and conservator so the director may apply the standard means test.

headings.title: Conservator payment of charges and discharge option
headings.reviewNote: Requires the conservator to pay assessed estate charges upon director notice and permits chapter 31 discharge after reasonable delay if the conservator fails to pay.

headings.title: Finality, circuit court appeal, and pre-discharge notice
headings.reviewNote: Makes the director's decision final subject to chapter 536 circuit court appeal, requires thirty days' notice to the conservator and supervising court before chapter 31 discharge, and stays discharge pending appeal.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires probate court notice of patient estates, directs standard means test assessment against estates, mandates conservator payment, and regulates pre-discharge notice and appeals.

headings.title: Definition of money for patient fund custody
headings.reviewNote: Defines money for section 630.305 to include legal tender, notes, drafts, certificates of deposit, stocks, bonds, checks, and credit cards.

headings.title: Facility custody and accounting for patient money
headings.reviewNote: Permits department residential facilities to require turning over patient money for safekeeping and individual accounting, with turnover to conservators or parents on request except representative payee funds under section 630.315.

headings.title: Patient access to account money and policies
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees patients and residents easy access to account money for canteen and small purchases and requires written facility access policies approved by the department.

headings.title: Permissive restrictions to prevent asset dissipation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facilities under department policies to deny account access when essential to prevent significant asset dissipation or protect safety, while allowing non-dissipative spending.

headings.title: Financial institution deposits and depositary bidding
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing patient money in financial institutions selected by bidding under sections 110.070 to 110.110 and crediting attributable earnings to each patient's account.

headings.title: Delivery of account money upon release
headings.reviewNote: Requires delivering all account money and earnings upon release to the patient, conservator, or parent, while permitting continued depositary service for placement-program clients.

headings.title: Department safeguards and principal guarantee
headings.reviewNote: Requires department policies safeguarding patient accounts against theft, loss, or misappropriation and guarantees the principal amounts in each account.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines money and governs facility safekeeping, accounting, patient access, asset-dissipation restrictions, depositary bidding, release delivery, and principal guarantees for patient funds.

headings.title: Diligent refund of departed patient personal funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility heads to use proper diligence to refund unclaimed personal funds of deceased, released, or escaped patients to them or heirs, allowing probate disposition or claims for unmet care costs.

headings.title: One-year escheat of unclaimed patient funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs that after one year, unclaimed funds under one hundred dollars vest immediately in the Mental Health Trust Fund, while funds of one hundred dollars or more go to a general revenue escheat account for two years before vesting in the trust fund.

headings.title: Cole County circuit court claims for escheated funds
headings.reviewNote: Permits claimants within two years of deposit to petition the Cole County circuit court for escheated funds of one hundred dollars or more without interest or costs, with civil appeal rights.

headings.title: Exemption for funds due state for support
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that section 630.320 does not apply to funds regularly due the state of Missouri for patient support and maintenance.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs diligent refund efforts, one-year escheat procedures to the Mental Health Trust Fund or escheat account, two-year Cole County court claims, and support-fund exemptions for unclaimed patient funds.

headings.title: Acceptance of gifts and Mental Health Trust Fund creation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to accept and hold grants, gifts, escheated moneys, and property in trust, convey or lease real property if authorized by the general assembly, and creates the nonreverting Mental Health Trust Fund.

headings.title: Restrictions on appropriating Mental Health Trust Fund
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits appropriating Mental Health Trust Fund moneys in lieu of general revenues and restricts appropriations to donor objects or special projects and equipment from section 630.320 escheated moneys.

headings.title: Annual written report on Mental Health Trust Fund
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to submit an annual written report on Mental Health Trust Fund moneys to the governor, commissioner of administration, and general assembly within ninety days after fiscal year close.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes acceptance of gifts, bequests, and donations, creating the Mental Health Trust Fund for administration.

headings.title: Establishment of facility canteens and commissaries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the head of any department mental health or developmental disability facility or regional center, with director approval, to establish and operate a canteen or commissary for patients, residents, and employees.

headings.title: Canteen revenue accounts and trust fund deposits
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate facility accounts for canteen operating costs, monthly deposit of remaining sales funds into the nonreverting Mental Health Trust Fund, and appropriation for facility recreation, habilitation, or treatment.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes department facilities and regional centers to operate canteens and commissaries and regulates separate revenue accounts and monthly Mental Health Trust Fund deposits.

headings.title: Establishment of facility vocational activity centers
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the head of any department mental health or intellectual disability facility or regional center, with director approval, to establish a vocational activity center for patients or residents.

headings.title: Activity center accounts and general revenue deposits
headings.reviewNote: Requires separate accounts for activity center material and operating costs and monthly deposit of remaining sales funds into the state general revenue fund.

headings.title: Limitation regarding off-grounds sheltered workshops
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that this section does not authorize an on-grounds activity center for patients or residents who could participate in an off-grounds sheltered workshop under sections 178.900 to 178.960.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes facility vocational activity centers, regulates separate revenue accounts and general revenue deposits, and restricts on-grounds centers where off-grounds sheltered workshops are available.

headings.title: Purchase of services from external vendors
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to contract with public and private vendors to purchase community mental health, disability, and substance services.

headings.title: Scope of community services purchased by contract
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that purchased services include diagnosis, evaluation, treatment, habilitation, rehabilitation, and transportation.

headings.title: Purchasing rules and technical service authorizations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commissioner of administration in consultation with the director to promulgate purchasing rules under chapter 34.

headings.title: Remedial measures for Family Care Safety Registry failures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rules permitting contract suspension, termination, or sanctions against vendors failing to comply with background screening laws.

headings.title: Waiver of competitive bidding procedures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commissioner of administration to waive chapter 34 bidding procedures when services are best purchased directly.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under administrative procedures act
headings.reviewNote: Requires all purchasing rules promulgated under this section to comply with statutory rulemaking provisions under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs state purchase of services from private and public vendors, purchasing procedures, employee screening compliance, and bidding waivers.

headings.title: Recognition criteria for administrative entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department recognition of county boards, service consortiums, and targeted case management providers as administrative entities.

headings.title: Direct contracting without competitive bidding
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes direct department contracts with recognized administrative entities without requiring competitive bidding under state purchasing laws.

headings.title: Delegated subcontracting authority for state facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs delegation of subcontracting authority to state facility administrative entities to provide comprehensive treatment consortiums.

headings.title: Access to state contracts for medical supplies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes administrative entities to utilize state purchasing contracts for pharmaceuticals and medical supplies when permitted.

headings.title: Exclusion from state legal expense fund
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that administrative entity recognition does not confer coverage under the state legal expense fund or sovereign immunity statutes.

headings.title: Rulemaking for entity designation and revocation
headings.reviewNote: Directs promulgation of regulations governing designation, contracting, and revocation of administrative entities.

entries.reviewSummary: Recognizes administrative entities, authorizes direct noncompetitive contracts, allows supply contract access, and regulates entity designations.

headings.title: Geographic service units in purchase contracts
headings.reviewNote: Requires purchase-of-service contracts to specify accessible units of service within defined geographic areas.

headings.title: Evidence of cost-and-benefit effectiveness required
headings.reviewNote: Directs contract monitoring requiring vendors to demonstrate that state-funded services are cost-and-benefit effective.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires contracted services to define geographic service units and mandates monitoring evidence of cost-and-benefit effectiveness.

headings.title: Incentive grants for unserved and underserved areas
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes grants to public and private entities to establish facilities and programs in underserved areas of the state.

headings.title: Rulemaking for grant monitoring and auditing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules establishing procedures for monitoring and auditing incentive-grant projects.

headings.title: Duration and renewal of incentive grants
headings.reviewNote: Limits incentive grants to one year with renewal permitted for only one additional year subject to appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes incentive grants to establish community facilities in underserved areas, directs audit rules, and limits grant duration.

headings.title: Rulemaking for incentive-grant contracting procedures
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commissioner of administration in consultation with the director to promulgate rules governing incentive-grant contracts.

headings.title: Demonstration of cost-and-benefit effectiveness
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipients of state incentive grants to provide evidence that funded programs are cost-and-benefit effective.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs purchasing rules for incentive grants and requires evidence that supported programs are cost-and-benefit effective.

headings.title: Financial record keeping by vendors and grantees
headings.reviewNote: Requires vendors and grantees to maintain records fully disclosing funding receipts, total project costs, and matching funds.

headings.title: Audit access by department and state auditor
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department and state auditor full access to recipient books, documents, and records pertinent to state funding.

headings.title: Confidentiality of recipient identities during audits
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department and state auditor to perform auditing functions in a manner that keeps individual service-recipient identities confidential under state and federal law.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates vendor and grantee financial record keeping, department and state auditor audit access, and protection of service-recipient identity confidentiality during audits.

headings.title: Definition of vendor overpayment
headings.reviewNote: Defines overpayment as payments exceeding allowable costs or services determined upon departmental audit or review.

headings.title: Certified written notice of overpayment and demand
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice of overpayment by certified mail stating the amount and basis and requesting prompt reimbursement.

headings.title: Assessment of interest on delinquent balances
headings.reviewNote: Assesses interest on unpaid overpayment balances beginning forty-five days after notice at statutory interest rates.

headings.title: Negotiation of structured repayment plans
headings.reviewNote: Provides forty-five days from notice receipt to negotiate a repayment plan over a period not exceeding twelve months from final disposition of any review, by direct payment, deduction from future amounts due, or both.

headings.title: Administrative offset and collection referrals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes offsetting future payments or referring delinquent overpayment balances to collection after six months.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines overpayments, establishes certified written notice, interest assessments, repayment plan negotiations, and offset remedies.

headings.title: Transfer of discontinued facility property
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes transfer of unused department facility buildings and real property to other state departments or agencies.

headings.title: Director approval required for property transfer
headings.reviewNote: Requires the governor to obtain approval from the mental health director prior to transferring facility real property.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes transfer of discontinued facility buildings and property to other state agencies upon gubernatorial and director approval.

headings.title: Lease-purchase agreements for facility construction
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commissioner of administration to execute lease-purchase contracts for facilities constructed on department grounds.

headings.title: Attorney general approval of conveyance instruments
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general to approve the legal form of all conveyance instruments executed under lease-purchase contracts.

headings.title: Prevailing wage requirement for construction workers
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that construction contractors and subcontractors pay not less than the prevailing wage rate under chapter 290.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes lease-purchase agreements for private construction on facility grounds, legal deed approval, and prevailing wage mandates.

headings.title: Establishment of centralized supply warehouses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to operate or contract for centralized warehouses to store and distribute supplies to department facilities.

headings.title: Establishment of Mental Health Central Supply Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the revolving Mental Health Central Supply Fund in the state treasury to finance supply warehouse operations.

headings.title: Issuance of supply commodities to facilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs the issuance of warehouse supply commodities to department facilities and administrative units upon requisition.

headings.title: Appropriation billing for issued commodities
headings.reviewNote: Requires charges for distributed commodities to be paid from appropriations made to requisitioning facilities and units.

headings.title: Administration of supply fund and cash flow reserves
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to administer the fund and adjust commodity charges to maintain necessary cash flow balances.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes central supply warehouses, creates the Mental Health Central Supply Fund, and regulates commodity billing and cash flow balances.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of eating disorder council
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Eating Disorder Council within the department comprising clinicians, researchers, advocacy groups, and the public.

headings.title: Duties and responsibilities of eating disorder council
headings.reviewNote: Tasks the council with overseeing awareness programs, assessing statewide treatment availability, and identifying research projects.

headings.title: Council member terms and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides four-year staggered terms and authorizes actual and necessary expense reimbursement without compensation.

headings.title: Organizational meetings and election of council officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires an initial organizational meeting, election of chair and vice chair, and subsequent meetings on call.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Eating Disorder Council, defining membership composition, duties, staggered terms, expenses, and meetings.

headings.title: Development of eating disorder education programs
headings.reviewNote: Directs interagency development of training programs for healthcare providers, school professionals, and general public awareness.

headings.title: Interagency cooperation for program implementation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to seek cooperation and assistance from other state departments to implement educational programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs interagency development of eating disorder education programs for healthcare and education professionals and public awareness.

headings.title: Referrals for placement out of facilities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that facility heads refer patients for community placement and reclassify placed individuals as department clients.

headings.title: Persons authorized to apply for placement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes patients, parents of minors, guardians, courts, or state and private custodial agencies to apply for placement.

headings.title: Comprehensive evaluation and placement criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs comprehensive evaluations and individualized plans, requiring diagnosed disorders and barring placements solely for special education.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs referrals for placement out of facilities, direct placement applications, comprehensive evaluations, and eligibility criteria.

headings.title: Authorized residential placement settings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes placement in licensed social services homes, certified department facilities, or the client's own home following consultation.

headings.title: Secure facility placement for criminal commitments
headings.reviewNote: Requires chapter 552 criminal acquittees for dangerous felonies to be placed in secure facilities absent court orders.

headings.title: Written statement of placement appropriateness
headings.reviewNote: Requires written statements explaining placement appropriateness to clients, guardians, courts, and prosecuting attorneys for criminal commitments.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs placement options in licensed facilities or homes, secure placement for criminal commitments, and written appropriateness notices.

headings.title: Objection to placement from developmental facility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the head of a developmental disability facility, when a resident, parent, or guardian refuses placement consent, to petition the division director under section 633.135 to determine appropriateness.

headings.title: Objection to placement from psychiatric facility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the head of a mental health facility, when a patient, parent, or guardian refuses placement consent, to petition the division of comprehensive psychiatric services director to determine appropriateness.

headings.title: Appointment of independent hearing panel
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division advisory council chairman to appoint a three-member review panel including at least one family member or guardian of a department facility patient and nongovernmental mental health organization members, excluding department officers or employees.

headings.title: Hearing procedures and appropriateness determination
headings.reviewNote: Directs the panel to conduct recorded hearings and determine placement appropriateness under statutory criteria.

headings.title: Judicial review of director decision in court
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes patients, parents, or guardians to appeal the director's placement decision to circuit court within thirty days.

headings.title: Application of administrative procedure rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that notice and hearing procedures before the placement review panel shall comply with chapter 536.

headings.title: Burden of proof on facility head
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of proof on the facility head to prove placement appropriateness by a preponderance of the evidence.

headings.title: Stay of placement pending final determination
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits placing or discharging the patient pending panel review and final director or court decision, except for temporary transfer in a medical emergency.

headings.title: Prohibition on retaliation against state employees
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits retaliation against state employees who participate in good faith placement decisions or testify at hearings.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes placement objection procedures, advisory council hearing panels, circuit court appeals, stay of placement, and retaliation bans.

headings.title: State funding for inadequate placement assistance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to pay community care, treatment, and room and board costs when public benefits are inadequate.

headings.title: Fee recovery from clients and liable relatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to charge clients or liable relatives for placement costs in accordance with statutory means tests.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes state payment of placement costs when public assistance is inadequate and directs fee recovery from liable parties.

headings.title: Rulemaking for residential and day program standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to promulgate rules setting reasonable standards for levels of service in residential and day programs.

headings.title: Classification of facilities and program services
headings.reviewNote: Provides that rules shall classify programs by client population, facility size, and types of specialized services offered.

headings.title: Substantive standards for admission and care
headings.reviewNote: Specifies standards governing diagnostic admission criteria, individualized treatment plans, personnel qualifications, safety, and records.

headings.title: Certification of qualifying facilities without fees
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to issue certification without charging a fee to facilities and programs meeting established standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs rules establishing standards for residential facilities, facility classifications, program criteria, and fee-free certification.

headings.title: Licensing standards for residential facilities and programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules establishing reasonable licensing standards for residential facilities and day programs serving persons with mental disorders.

headings.title: Classification of licensed facilities and programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires rules to reasonably classify facilities and programs by resident or client population, size, and service types to promote safe, humane, and adequate care.

headings.title: Exemptions from department licensing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Exempts facilities relying solely on prayer, facilities operated by health or social services, and accredited hospitals.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs licensing rules and standards for mental health facilities, facility classifications, and statutory licensing exemptions.

headings.title: Substantive licensing standards for facility operations
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensing standards covering admission criteria, treatment plans, staff qualifications, nutrition, sanitation, and safety.

headings.title: Small living unit classifications required
headings.reviewNote: Requires living units within facilities or homes to be classified in small sizes to ensure homelike environments.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies substantive licensing standards for admissions, treatment, staffing, and small living unit classifications.

headings.title: Licensing procedures and application standards
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishment of licensing procedures ensuring compliance with departmental standards and statutory provisions.

headings.title: Application requirements and graded license fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires license applications on department forms and establishes graded fees based on client capacity deposited into general revenue.

headings.title: Affidavit of truthfulness and document submission
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit sworn affidavits attesting to the truth of application statements and filed documents.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes licensing procedures, application forms, graded license fees, and verified applicant affidavits.

headings.title: Licensing exemption for exclusive substance abuse programs
headings.reviewNote: Exempts residential facilities and day programs providing services exclusively for substance abuse from department licensing rules.

headings.title: Submission of program description and fire-safety compliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires substance abuse programs to submit service descriptions and documentation of compliance with local fire-safety standards.

headings.title: Department survey and legislative fire-safety report
headings.reviewNote: Directs a department survey and report to the general assembly on bringing substance programs into fire-safety compliance.

headings.title: Disqualification from certification for failure to submit
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies facilities failing to submit required program and fire-safety information from receiving certification or state funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts exclusive substance abuse programs from licensure rules, requires fire-safety filings, surveys facilities, and penalizes noncompliance.

headings.title: Issuance of one-year facility license
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to issue a one-year license upon applicant demonstration of compliance with established rules.

headings.title: License renewal notices and filing deadlines
headings.reviewNote: Requires department renewal notices sixty days prior to expiration and application submission thirty days prior.

headings.title: Temporary operating permits pending inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to grant a temporary operating permit for relicensure inspection when the inspection is not completed before license expiration through no fault of the applicant.

headings.title: Non-transferability of license and ownership permits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that licenses are nontransferable and nonassignable without written department approval and requires granting a temporary operating permit to evaluate a change-of-ownership application.

headings.title: Conspicuous posting of facility license
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that issued licenses be displayed conspicuously on the licensed facility premises.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs one-year license issuance, renewal notices, temporary operating permits, non-transferability, and conspicuous posting.

headings.title: Revocation or denial of facility license
headings.reviewNote: Mandates license revocation or denial for substantial failure to comply with departmental standards or statutory requirements.
