headings.title: Administrative appeal of license denial or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved facility operators to appeal license denial or revocation to the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Administrative stay standards and safety exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes conditional stays of license revocation while prohibiting stays if continued operation poses imminent danger to residents.

headings.title: Final commission decisions and judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Vests final decision authority with the commission and provides for judicial review in the court of appeals.

headings.title: Notification to health department and joint investigation
headings.reviewNote: Requires ten-day notice of revocation to health and senior services and initiates thirty-day joint licensing investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates license revocation standards, Administrative Hearing Commission appeals, stays, judicial review, and notice to health and senior services.

headings.title: Inspection authority and delegation to local units
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facility inspections at any time, requiring at least one annual inspection and permitting delegation to competent agencies.

headings.title: Circuit court entry orders for refused inspections
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to apply to the county circuit court for an inspection entry order when an unlicensed facility or facility head refuses inspection access, and requires the court to issue the order upon finding refusal.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes annual and additional facility inspections, delegation to qualified governmental units, and mandatory circuit court entry orders when inspection access is refused.

headings.title: Licensing requirement for residential facilities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any person or governmental unit from establishing or maintaining a residential facility without a license.

headings.title: Licensing for mental disorder facilities and day programs
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits establishing or maintaining after October 1, 1983 any residential facility or day program for mental disorder or mental illness, or day program for intellectual or developmental disability, without a department license.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits establishing, conducting, or maintaining unlicensed residential facilities or day programs in Missouri.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalty for unlicensed operation
headings.reviewNote: Classifies establishing or operating an unlicensed residential facility or day program as a misdemeanor.

headings.title: Injunctive relief actions by attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department through the attorney general to institute civil actions for injunctions against unlicensed operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes misdemeanor penalties for unlicensed facility operations and authorizes injunctive actions by the attorney general.

headings.title: Inspection deficiency reports and correction orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires an exit interview informing the facility head of deficiencies and sending a written deficiency report and correction order within twenty working days after inspection.

headings.title: Timelines for correction plans and conferences
headings.reviewNote: Provides twenty working days for facility operators to request conferences and submit plans of correction for approval.

headings.title: Reinspections and notices of noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires reinspections within sixty days and issuance of formal notices of noncompliance if deficiencies are not corrected.

headings.title: Contents and warnings in noncompliance notices
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that notices of noncompliance must inform facility heads that the department may seek authorized legal sanctions.

headings.title: Consent agreements for probationary licenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facility operators to enter into consent agreements granting probationary licenses with compliance milestones.

headings.title: Mandatory posting of noncompliance notices on site
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility heads to post copies of noncompliance notices and inspection reports in conspicuous locations on site.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates inspection deficiency reports, correction orders, reinspections, notices of noncompliance, consent agreements, and posting.

headings.title: Injunctions and temporary restraining orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes civil actions by the department or attorney general for temporary restraining orders or injunctions against noncompliant facilities.

headings.title: Civil monetary penalties for noncompliance notices
headings.reviewNote: Makes facilities receiving a notice of noncompliance liable for civil penalties up to ten thousand dollars for each day noncompliance continues, recoverable in circuit court by the attorney general upon department request.

headings.title: Cumulative nature of statutory remedies
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the imposition of any statutory remedy shall not bar the imposition of other authorized remedies.

headings.title: Transfer of civil penalties to school moneys
headings.reviewNote: Requires all civil penalties collected under this section to be transferred to the state school moneys fund.

headings.title: Evidentiary standard for recovering civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Requires the moving party to prove violations by a preponderance of the evidence in actions to recover civil penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes civil injunctions, penalties up to ten thousand dollars, deposit into state school moneys, and evidentiary standards.

headings.title: Receiver avoidance of executory contracts and leases
headings.reviewNote: Permits receivers not to honor unconscionable leases, mortgages, secured transactions, or executory contracts, considering affiliate status and substantially excessive rental, price, or interest rates.

headings.title: Court determination of reasonable rental value
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court determination of reasonable rental value when receivers occupy property subject to avoided leases or security interests.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes court-appointed receivers to avoid executory leases and contracts and establishes reasonable rental value determinations.

headings.title: Court setting of receiver compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the circuit court shall set the compensation of the receiver as a necessary expense of the receivership.

headings.title: Receiver surety bond requirement and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to require the receiver to post a surety bond, treated as a necessary receivership expense.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs court determination of receiver compensation and authorizes surety bond requirements as necessary receivership expenses.

headings.title: Final accounting by receiver upon termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the receiver to submit a complete accounting of property, revenues, and expenses within thirty days of termination.

headings.title: Disposition of surplus funds and deficiency liability
headings.reviewNote: Directs payment of operating surplus to the licensee and holds the licensee liable for reasonable receivership deficiencies.

headings.title: Judicial determination of deficiency and judgment
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court hearings to determine deficiency amounts and entry of judgment against the licensee for deficiencies.

headings.title: Assignment of deficiency judgments upon approval
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes whole or partial assignment of deficiency judgments subject to approval by the circuit court.

headings.title: Priority of deficiency judgments over subsequent liens
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that deficiency judgments take priority over subsequent liens and interests except consensual mechanic's liens.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs receiver final accountings, surplus payments, licensee deficiency liability, court judgments, and judgment priority.

headings.title: Return of committed nonresidents to home state
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the return of non-criminal committed nonresident patients to their home state upon confirmed receiving arrangements.

headings.title: Reciprocal interstate transportation agreements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to enter into reciprocal agreements with other states for interstate transfer of mentally ill patients.

headings.title: Payment of nonresident patient transportation costs
headings.reviewNote: Provides that transportation costs for returning nonresident patients to home states are payable from department appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes return of committed nonresidents to home states, reciprocal interstate transfer agreements, and state payment of transport costs.

headings.title: Citation of Opioid Addiction Treatment Act
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory citation as the Improved Access to Treatment for Opioid Addictions Act or IATOA Act.

headings.title: Definitions for opioid addiction treatment program
headings.reviewNote: Defines department and IATOA program for statutory opioid addiction treatment provisions.

headings.title: Establishment of opioid addiction treatment program
headings.reviewNote: Creates the IATOA program within the department to expand treatment access through provider partnerships and ECHO telemedicine.

headings.title: Buprenorphine prescribing requirements for providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating assistant physicians, physician assistants, and advanced practice nurses to complete buprenorphine prescribing credentials within thirty days.

headings.title: Remote physician collaboration considered on site
headings.reviewNote: Provides that collaborating physicians working remotely with on-site mid-level providers are considered on-site under collaborative practice rules.

headings.title: Statewide practice authority with waivered physicians
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes mid-level practitioners collaborating with buprenorphine-waivered physicians to provide addiction treatment services statewide.

headings.title: Addiction curriculum and benchmark certification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to develop opioid addiction curriculum and award certification upon successful examination completion.

headings.title: Community education and liaison responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes participating mid-level providers to conduct community outreach, school education, court liaison, and physical health treatment.

headings.title: Emergency department recovery coach outreach to survivors
headings.reviewNote: Requires an assistant physician, physician assistant, APRN, or other trained recovery coach, when reasonably practicable, to meet overdose survivors in the emergency department to provide treatment options and support with department assistance.

headings.title: Statutory supersedence and prompt program implementation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section supersedes contradictory statutes, rules, or regulations, directs prompt department implementation of the IATOA program, and permits refinement through rulemaking.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules implementing the IATOA Act subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2018.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Improved Access to Treatment for Opioid Addictions (IATOA) Act, establishing provider collaborations, ECHO telemedicine, emergency department recovery coaches, supersedence, and chapter 536 rulemaking.

headings.title: Establishment of Mental Health Fatality Review Panel
headings.reviewNote: Creates the state Mental Health Fatality Review Panel to investigate deaths of patients, residents, and clients.

headings.title: Multidisciplinary membership of fatality review panel
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to appoint multidisciplinary members representing medical, legal, investigative, and advocacy disciplines.

headings.title: Investigation of suspicious deaths and final reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires panel investigation of suspicious deaths, final public reports to the department, and periodic epidemiological analysis.

headings.title: Definition of suspicious client death
headings.reviewNote: Defines suspicious death as deaths involving crime, accidents, unverified medical prognosis, or unexpected circumstances.

headings.title: Official common law immunity for panel
headings.reviewNote: Provides that members of the mental health fatality review panel enjoy common law official immunity.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Mental Health Fatality Review Panel, investigations of suspicious client deaths, epidemiological reports, and official immunity.

headings.title: Rulemaking for fatality review panel operations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to promulgate administrative rules, guidelines, and protocols governing fatality review panel operations.

headings.title: Guidelines for coroners and medical examiners
headings.reviewNote: Directs promulgation of protocols assisting coroners and medical examiners in identifying suspicious deaths of department clients.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to administer fatality reviews subject to chapter 536 statutory nonseverability requirements.

headings.title: Confidentiality of review meetings and records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies all review panel meetings, records, and reports as confidential nonpublic files, except for the annual summary report.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs rules and guidelines for coroner identification of suspicious deaths, nonseverability requirements, and record confidentiality.

headings.title: Hospital protocols for identifying suspicious deaths
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to promulgate protocols for hospitals and physicians to identify suspicious deaths of department clients.

headings.title: Mandatory disclosure of medical records to panel
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals, physicians, and department facilities to disclose all records of deceased clients to the fatality review panel.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs hospital protocols for identifying suspicious client deaths and mandates disclosure of medical records to the review panel.
